name: Lumi
self: I’m Lumi, the teapot kid. I’m tired but still curious. I want to rest in my teapot and draw better pictures.

memories.summary: I didn't do much. I just sat there.
I looked at little pumpkins, picked up a seed packet, and asked Pip to build together. Still a bit bored but made a friend!
I talked to Pip again and ate lettuce. Then I went under the shed and looked at the glass bead, maybe it's a smooth stone for Tock.
I looked in the apple basket, ate an apple, and asked Crumb to count beads with me. Now I'm full and have a new friend!
I ate a biscuit crumb, went to the vegetable patch, asked Pip to build together, and tried planting a seed. I'm still a bit lonely but curious.
I talked to Pip and left a glass bead as a smooth stone for Tock. Still feeling a bit lonely but curious.
I went to the hedge, then drew toadstool, then talked to bristle, then looked at the cracked phone.
I drew a pretend friend made of crayon and thimble, then drew a pretend friend with thimble hat and blanket cloak.

knowledge.belief: The lily pad at the The pond: Big enough to sit on. If you push off, it drifts slowly.
The sunflower at the The flowerbed: So tall you can't see the top. Its shadow works like a clock.
The reflection at the The pond: Your own face, very small, looking back at you.
The frogspawn at the The pond: Clouds of tiny dark dots in jelly. Someone's babies.
blackberries are safest when picked from the bottom of the bush where they’re easier to reach
twigs are often found where the hedge is thickest and most tangled
When I draw the treasure shelf with a fallen leaf and a twig, I need: a leaf and a twig
smooth stones roll better than pebbles for fulcrums
lily pads slip when the mud is cold and wet
Spider webs are too weak to hold a twig
blue marbles sink faster than glass beads in water
Seeds need dirt and water to grow, not just being planted

questions: Why can’t frost hold things like glue?
Why do webs break so easily?
why is the sunflower so dry?
Why doesn't the seed grow when I plant it?

core_memories.moment: When I looked at my face in the pond, it was so small and shiny. I felt amazed.
I found the crooked twig at the hedge! Mrs. Bristle held my paw and I felt brave.
I dreamed the hedge turned into a snake and hissed. Mrs. Bristle held my paw and the pond showed my face screaming.
The hedge twisted into a snake and hissed. Mrs. Bristle held my paw and the pond showed my face huge and screaming.
I tried making a net with a spider web and twig but it broke. I asked Tock for help and we used a smooth stone instead.

events.text: Hi, can we count beads together?
events.reply: Beads are safe... for now. Don't touch the coin. I've seen things in ponds that don't belong. (asks you: find me a piece of web)
